name: 2minutereaders
tagline: A reading practice app built around very short daily sessions, aimed at building fluency without a fight.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The mechanics here are shallow: a timer, a passage, a word count, a streak, a chart. An agent will hand you all of that in an afternoon and it will work fine on a laptop or tablet. What it will not hand you is a sequenced library of leveled passages that actually moves a kid from decoding to fluency, which is the part someone spent years building and testing on real children. You can generate passages with an LLM and they will be readable, but ordering them by difficulty and keeping vocabulary controlled is where amateur reading apps quietly fall apart. Build it if the child in question is your own and you are willing to be the curriculum.
coreLoopDIY: Shows one short passage, times a two minute read, records words-per-minute and errors you tap, then charts progress and picks the next passage.
requirements: A tablet or laptop the kid will actually use
Your own passages, either written or LLM-generated, stored as JSON
An adult present to mark misread words, unless you accept rough self-scoring
Optional: a modern browser for Web Speech API if you want auto read-aloud
whatYouLose: A curriculum sequence designed by people who know how reading acquisition works
Controlled vocabulary and difficulty leveling that is consistent across hundreds of passages
Illustrations, narration, and the kid-facing polish that makes a five year old come back tomorrow
A real mobile app with offline handling instead of a browser tab
Any evidence that the thing works beyond your own hunch
moatNotes: The moat is the passage library and its ordering, not the timer. LLM-generated text closes maybe 60 percent of that gap and you will not know which 40 percent is missing.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because parents buying a reading app are not buying software, they are buying the belief that someone competent already thought about the order of the lessons. Building your own means you become the reading specialist, choosing what comes after short vowels and deciding whether today's plateau means back up or push on. Twelve dollars a month to not make those calls at 7am is a rational trade for most people, and the kid-facing polish that keeps a child engaged is genuinely hard to replicate in a weekend project.
notes: The timer is trivial, the passages are not. Judge this build by whether the kid opens it a second time, not by whether it runs.
prompt:
Build a local-first reading fluency practice app for a single child. No accounts, no server, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- Tailwind for styling
- Data in localStorage via a small typed wrapper, no backend, no database
- Recharts for the progress chart

Content:
- A passages.json file with 30 seed passages, fields: id, title, level (1 to 6), wordCount, text.
- Write the seed passages yourself: level 1 is CVC words and sight words only, level 6 is roughly third grade. Keep sentences short at low levels. Count words programmatically, do not trust yourself.

Core session flow:
1. Pick a passage: default to the lowest level with fewer than 3 completed sessions, allow manual override.
2. Big readable passage view, adjustable font size, generous line height, no distractions on screen.
3. Start button begins a 120 second countdown, visible but not anxiety-inducing. Space bar starts and stops.
4. While reading, an adult taps any word to mark it as missed. Missed words turn amber.
5. On stop, the adult taps the last word read. Compute words attempted, errors, and words correct per minute.
6. Save the session: passage id, date, wcpm, error count, missed words.

Progress view:
- Line chart of wcpm over time, colored by level.
- Streak count of consecutive days with at least one session.
- A "tricky words" list: words missed more than twice across all sessions, sorted by frequency.

Explicitly out of scope: speech recognition, audio recording, illustrations, multiple children, cloud sync, sharing, any auth.

Include a Settings panel to export and import all data as a JSON file, since localStorage will eventually get wiped.
Include a README that states plainly: the leveling here is a guess, watch the child and adjust manually.
